## Default register

| Choice | Current value | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nested ML score projection and LR spectrum | Observed geometry | Adopted; confirmatory calibration open | Smoke and pilot check construction and compute cost only |
| Global ML geometry | Expected | Outside this decision | No change proposed |

## Question

Does observed nested ML geometry calibrate at least as well as expected geometry,
particularly when the larger model is misspecified?

## Short answer

Confirmation has not run. The pilot prices the registered 16-cell study and checks
that the observed arm reproduces the ordinary policy. Its rejection rates cannot
justify a geometry decision.

```{r}
out <- file.path('results', 'nested-geometry', 'pilot')
if (!file.exists(file.path(out, 'timing.csv')))
  stop('Pilot results absent. Run Rscript run_experiment.R --pilot with the lane library.')
timing <- read.csv(file.path(out, 'timing.csv'))
checks <- read.csv(file.path(out, 'checks.csv'))
metadata <- read.csv(file.path(out, 'metadata.csv'))
hours <- sum(timing$production_cpu_hours)
knitr::kable(data.frame(`Production CPU Hours` = round(hours, 2),
  `Ideal Four Core Hours` = round(hours / 4, 2), `Pilot Draws` = checks$draws,
  `Failed Arms` = checks$failed_arms, `Maximum Policy Gap` = checks$max_policy_gap),
  check.names = FALSE)
```

## Evidence and decision rule

The registered [criteria](criteria/nested_geometry.md) compare expected and
observed score and LR quadratics, each with SB and PEBA4. A two-group CFA tests
six loading restrictions. Equal population loadings make the null hold both
under the correct larger model and under an omitted residual covariance shared
by both groups. Normal and Vale–Maurelli skewed indicators are studied at 100
and 300 observations per group; power lowers group b's standardized x3 loading
by .15.

Retain the observed geometry unless, in some misspecified-larger-model null cell, its PEBA4 or SB size error exceeds the expected geometry's by more than 1 percentage point with a paired 95% interval excluding zero. Report correct-model cells as controls; there both geometries are consistent. Size-adjusted power is reported, not gating.

Per-cell Wilson intervals, paired bootstrap intervals, failures, matching-null
p-value critical values and size-adjusted power are in the run's summary CSVs.
Production has 2000 null and 1000 power replicates per cell (24000 draws).
Both fits use ordinary default ML estimation and library convergence verdicts;
the quadratics reuse one shared prepared inference dataset.

## Caveats

Twenty draws per cell assess mechanics and timing, not one-percentage-point
size differences. Four-core pricing assumes ideal scaling; worker startup,
summary computation and remote billing overhead add time. No Modal price model
was available in this session, so the estimate is CPU-hours only. Generator
calibration is included in the measured per-draw cost. Complete-pair inference
conditions on available tests; all failures remain separately visible.

## Reproduce

Use the installed lane-c library; one math thread per worker:

```bash
export R_LIBS="$HOME/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-c"
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1
nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --help
nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --smoke --run-id new_smoke
nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --pilot --run-id new_pilot
quarto render report.qmd
```

After the task-43 compute decision, the production command is
`nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --production --workers 4`.
Each run uses a fresh output directory and separate mode seeds. Raw batches
stay local; frozen pilot summaries and source/native fingerprints provide
pricing provenance. Earlier failed smoke attempts remain local diagnostics.
